title: Does Your Cat's Litter-Box Parasite Make You Crash Motorcycles or Pitch Startups? — Berdoy & Sapolsky's Rodent Medial-Amygdala "Fatal Feline Attraction", Toxoplasma Profilin TLR11 Divergence (PDB 3NEC), Rhoptry Kinase ROP18 (PDB 3DZO) & TgAaaH2/BH4 Recycling (PDB 2V6S), and Flegr/Johnson Crash & Entrepreneurship ORs vs. Sugden's Prospective Dunedin Birth-Cohort Null

teenKit.tldr: A microscopic parasite from cat litter boxes sneaks into human brains, and wild studies claim it might make you riskier—driving you to launch startups or crash cars.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It forces us to question how much of our free will and bold personality traits are actually controlled by tiny hitchhiking microbes.
keyTakeaways: Toxoplasma gondii is a common protozoan parasite that reproduces in cats but can infect humans through contaminated litter boxes or food.
Observational studies have linked carrying the parasite to higher rates of entrepreneurship, business majors, and traffic accidents due to altered risk-taking behavior.
While catchy headlines claim the parasite rewires human ambition, rigorous gold-standard birth cohort studies sometimes find a null effect, reminding us to question dramatic correlations.

vocab.meaning: A tiny, crescent-shaped single-celled parasite famous for living in cat intestines and manipulating host behavior.
